outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the constant-2 inequality has been claimed proved by three unrefereed 2026 preprints: Shanmu Jin (first posted 27 July 2026, all polynomials then reportedly all holomorphic f), Emiel Lorist and Felix Schwenninger (arXiv 4 August 2026, rational f), and Qinyu Luo (late August 2026, polynomials and rational functions). No peer-reviewed resolution was found, and I could read the full text of only one of the three, so the status rests on the authors' own arXiv text for that one and on secondary reports for the others.
problem_asks: (1) For every complex square matrix A of any size n; the statement sets no size. (2) For every complex function f for which f(A) is defined; the statement names no class, and the literature restricts to functions holomorphic on a neighbourhood of the field of values W(A). The 2026 claims variously cover polynomials, rational functions, or such holomorphic functions. (3) The norm of f(A), which the statement calls the matrix norm; the literature means the operator (spectral) norm. (4) The inequality ‖f(A)‖ ≤ 2 · sup over z in W(A) of |f(z)|. Part (a): the inequality holds at all for every such A and f. Part (b): the constant is exactly 2, not a larger constant such as the known 1+√2. Not asked by the statement but discussed in the literature: that 2 is sharp (conjectured, and claimed optimal in the 2026 preprints), and the matrix-valued (completely bounded) form, which the statement does not mention.

events.what_happened: Crouzeix proved a dimension-independent bound with constant 11.08 in place of 2 for the functional-calculus inequality over the numerical range, published in the Journal of Functional Analysis (per the Wikipedia status article, which dates it 15 March 2007). The preprint date was not established.
events.delivers: A bound ‖f(A)‖ ≤ 11.08 · sup over W(A) of |f| for every A and f in the functional-calculus class, dimension-independent (per Wikipedia).
events.remains: The constant 2. Superseded by the 2017 Crouzeix–Palencia constant 1+√2.

checked_by.who: Referees of the Journal of Functional Analysis
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted for publication (journal date only; the review itself is not visible)

events.direction: Partial result toward the conjecture: an inequality of the right form with a larger constant.

events.what_happened: Crouzeix and Palencia showed that the numerical range of a linear operator on a Hilbert space is a complete (1+√2)-spectral set, with a short argument based on the Cauchy transform of conjugates of holomorphic functions. First public version: arXiv:1702.00668, submitted 2 February 2017, titled 'The numerical range as a spectral set'. Published as SIAM J. Matrix Anal. Appl. 38(2) (2017), 649–655 (DOI 10.1137/17M1116672).
events.revisions: arXiv v1 only (2 Feb 2017). Journal version SIMAX 2017 (Wikipedia dates it 7 June 2017).
events.delivers: For a bounded operator on a Hilbert space (including any n×n matrix A), the numerical range W(A) is a complete (1+√2)-spectral set, so ‖f(A)‖ ≤ (1+√2) · sup over W(A) of |f| for f holomorphic near W(A).
events.remains: The constant 2 of the conjecture. The gap between 2 and 1+√2 is the open part.

checked_by.who: SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications referees

events.direction: Partial result toward the conjecture: the same inequality shape with constant 1+√2 > 2. Wikipedia lists 2 ≤ C ≤ 1+√2 as the known range.

events.what_happened: O'Loughlin and Virtanen construct several classes of matrices, derived from a matrix satisfying the conjecture, for which the conjecture also holds. They also prove a link between cyclicity and the conjecture, and an if-and-only-if equivalence for 3×3 matrices with analytic truncated Toeplitz operators (arXiv:2306.12183).
events.delivers: Structural results and classes of matrices for which the conjecture holds; the classes are not named in the abstract. For symmetric 3×3 matrices the conjecture holds exactly when it holds for analytic truncated Toeplitz operators.
events.remains: The general conjecture for all matrices.
events.direction: Partial and structural, toward the conjecture. The abstract does not claim the constant 2 for any named class.

events.what_happened: Bickel, Corbett, Glenning, Guan and Vollmayr-Lee establish the level-set Crouzeix conjecture for several classes of 3×3, 4×4 and 5×5 matrices associated with compressions of the shift, and the full conjecture for several classes of nilpotent matrices (arXiv:2312.04537, submitted 7 December 2023). A journal version in Concrete Operators (December 2024) is reported by a search snippet (DOAJ listing); I did not open it.
events.revisions: v1 only (7 Dec 2023). Journal version Concrete Operators, Dec 2024, per snippet, unverified by me.
events.delivers: The full conjecture (constant 2) for several classes of nilpotent matrices; sizes not given in the abstract. For several classes of 3×3 to 5×5 compressions of the shift, only the weaker level-set version.
events.remains: All other matrices; the general conjecture.

checked_by.what_they_did: Journal publication reported by a search snippet; the review is not visible

events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture: proves it for restricted classes (nilpotent matrices), and the weaker level-set version for other classes.

events.what_happened: Malman, Mashreghi, O'Loughlin and Ransford study configuration constants of convex planar domains and improve the Crouzeix–Palencia constant for domains containing the numerical range (arXiv:2407.19049, first version 26 July 2024). The published venue is unresolved: Wikipedia cites IMRN (10 April 2025), while a search result links the same title to Integral Equations and Operator Theory (s00020-025-02800-2).
events.revisions: v1 26 Jul 2024; v2 27 Mar 2025 (the version on the arXiv page). Journal: unresolved (see what_happened).
events.delivers: For compact convex planar domains Ω with non-empty interior containing the numerical range, the Crouzeix–Palencia bound K ≤ 1+√2 is improved to K ≤ 1+√(1+a(Ω)), where a(Ω) < 1 for the analytic configuration constant, so the bound is strict for each such Ω. Also c_R(Ω) = c_C(Ω), and explicit estimates for ellipses in terms of eccentricity.
events.remains: The constant 2 for W(A). The improvement is domain-dependent, and the abstract I read does not state a uniform constant below 1+√2 over all Ω.
events.direction: Moves a neighbouring quantity (the spectral-set constant for convex domains Ω containing W(A)), not the constant 2 for W(A). Does not claim the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Malman, Mashreghi, O'Loughlin and Ransford bound the Crouzeix ratio for N×N matrices: the supremum of ‖p(A)‖ over polynomials bounded by 1 on W(A) (arXiv:2409.14127, submitted 21 September 2024). The abstract states the conjectured value 2 without proving it for any case.
events.delivers: For each fixed N, the Crouzeix ratio ψ(A) of an N×N matrix A is at most C_N, where C_N depends only on N and C_N < 1+√2. No explicit C_N is given in the abstract.
events.remains: The constant 2 for all N. The abstract does not say whether sup over N of C_N is below 1+√2; a uniform statement of that kind would be a further improvement, and I did not find one.
events.direction: Moves a bound for each matrix size, below 1+√2 but not to 2. Per size, a finite-dimensional family; the abstract does not claim 2 for any N.

events.what_happened: Crouzeix and Greenbaum give an alternative proof that the family of matrices studied by Choi (2013) satisfies Crouzeix's conjecture, and that the family satisfies the completely bounded version (arXiv:2508.12768, submitted 18 August 2025). The title refers to weighted shift matrices; the abstract defines the family only by reference to Choi's paper.
events.delivers: The constant-2 inequality, and its completely bounded version, for the Choi family of weighted shift matrices.
events.remains: All other matrices, and the general conjecture.
events.direction: Confirms the constant-2 inequality for a restricted class of matrices. Cuts toward the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Crouzeix posts 'Numerical Ranges and Spectral Sets: the unbounded case' (arXiv:2509.19792, submitted 24 September 2025). The abstract recalls that a convex set Ω containing W(A) is a spectral set for A with constant at most 1+√2, and says the estimate is improved in unbounded cases. I read the abstract page only.
events.delivers: An improvement of the 1+√2 spectral-set estimate for convex Ω containing W(A) in unbounded cases. The improved constant and the cases are not stated on the abstract page I read.
events.remains: The constant 2 for W(A), which the abstract does not mention.
events.direction: Neighbouring: a constant for convex domains Ω containing W(A), not for W(A) itself and not the value 2.

events.what_happened: O'Loughlin and Rani post 'q-Numerical Ranges and Spectral Sets' (arXiv:2603.15536, first submitted 16 March 2026; v2 3 October 2026). The abstract says it extends the Crouzeix–Palencia framework with a parameter, generalises the 1+√2 result to scaled q-numerical ranges, and formulates a generalisation of Crouzeix's conjecture for q-numerical ranges, with an application to GMRES.
events.delivers: Bounds for scaled q-numerical ranges, and a conjectured generalisation of Crouzeix's conjecture to q-numerical ranges. The abstract I read does not state the constant 2 for W(A).
events.remains: The constant-2 conjecture for W(A) itself.
events.direction: Analogue: the same kind of problem for q-numerical ranges. It is not a result on W(A) with constant 2.

events.what_happened: Shanmu Jin posts 'The Numerical Range Is a 2-Spectral Set' on Preprints.org (DOI 10.20944/preprints202607.1919.v1; submitted 24 July, posted 27 July 2026). Per its abstract as relayed by search snippets, for every complex polynomial p and n×n matrix A, ‖p(A)‖ ≤ 2 · max over W(A) of |p|, so W(A) is a 2-spectral set; the author claims this proves Crouzeix's conjecture and that the constant is optimal. Later versions (v3 5 Aug, v4 7 Aug) are reported to extend the estimate to every f holomorphic near W(A). I could not open any version: every Preprints.org fetch returned HTTP 403. The account below therefore rests on secondary reports that paraphrase the preprint and on snippets. The author is reported as a neurosurgery resident and postdoctoral researcher at Peking Union Medical College Hospital with no formal mathematics training.
events.revisions: v1 posted 27 Jul 2026 (title 'The Numerical Range Is a 2-Spectral Set'); v3 5 Aug 2026; v4 7 Aug 2026, cited by ingenieur.de as the current version. Breakthrough Tracker lists the manuscript as 'The Crouzeix Conjecture', revised through 7 Aug. Scope changed between versions per snippets (polynomials in v1; holomorphic f later).
events.delivers: Per the abstract as relayed: the constant-2 inequality for every polynomial p and every n×n A, so the numerical range is a 2-spectral set, and the constant is claimed optimal. Central tool as relayed: a positive-real completion theorem, and a matrix-valued Herglotz kernel evaluated at specially chosen points that cancels the completion term. Per snippets, later versions claim every f holomorphic near W(A).
events.remains: Nothing, on the author's claim. Whether the holomorphic-f extension is in the preprint I could not check.

events.what_happened: Emiel Lorist and Felix Schwenninger post 'A solution to Crouzeix's conjecture' on arXiv (arXiv:2608.03841, v1 4 August 2026, five pages per secondary reports; v2 17 August 2026). The v2 text gives the main result as Theorem 3, and its proof combines earlier tools for weaker estimates with a perturbation lemma for 2-dilations, applied to the iterates f^n in the double-layer potential representation. The authors state that they used GPT-5.6 Sol Pro through ChatGPT to explore proof strategies (quoted in ai). Their reference [17] is Jin's preprint, which they say they learned of on 28 July 2026, after the AI exploration on 25–26 July.
events.revisions: v1 4 Aug 2026 (7 KB); v2 17 Aug 2026 (10 KB). arXiv comments say v2 added a 'more detailed AI declaration'. Both versions' AI sentences are quoted in ai.
events.delivers: Per the v2 Theorem 3 as read in the arXiv HTML: for a bounded operator A on a Hilbert space, W(A) is a 2-spectral set, and for every rational function f with poles outside the closure of W(A), ‖f(A)‖ ≤ 2 · sup over W(A) of |f|. Matrices of every size are included as a special case. The v1 abstract states 'We provide a proof of Crouzeix's conjecture'.
events.remains: Holomorphic f that are not rational, unless a limiting argument not in the text I read extends the rational case. The completely bounded (matrix-valued) form is not claimed in the parts I read.

A secondary interview quotes Schwenninger as crediting Crouzeix and a third person for earlier pieces, while the v2 acknowledgements as paraphrased by the fetch tool name only two people; I did not verify the interview.

systems.name: GPT-5.6 Sol Pro
systems.what_it_did: Per the authors (v2): it 'was used on July 25 and 26, 2026, to review previous approaches to the weaker spectral constant and to identify a possible source of improvement in estimates involving iterates' of extremal or approximately extremal functions. The authors write: 'A key observation emerging from these interactions was that the discrepancy term ... can be controlled uniformly in n by the same quantity that naturally arises', and 'This yielded a preliminary result, from which Lemma 1 was subsequently abstracted.' The authors also write: 'The proof in its final form was developed in full, verified, and written by the authors.' Whether the model's observation is load-bearing is for the judging pass. The v1 disclosure names the model as 'ChatGPT 5.6 Pro by OpenAI'.

events.what_happened: Qinyu Luo posts 'Two Boundary-Certificate Proofs of the Crouzeix Theorem: Fiberwise Fourier Recurrence and Defect-Gram Telescoping' on Preprints.org (DOI 10.20944/preprints202608.1661.v2). Per the abstract as relayed by search snippets, it gives two proofs of the finite-dimensional scalar Crouzeix theorem, for polynomials and for rational functions without poles on W(A), and states that two pinned Lean 4 developments kernel-check the polynomial and reduced-rational endpoints. The affiliation in a snippet is ByteDance, Beijing. The Preprints.org page returned HTTP 403, so I did not read the full text.

events.what_happened: Per Åhag, Rafał Czyż and Jani Virtanen post 'The Complete Crouzeix Conjecture in Dimension Three and the Clouâtre–Ostermann–Ransford conjecture' (arXiv:2608.27346). The abstract says they settle the complete Crouzeix conjecture for matrices of order at most three; prove the Q-algebra case of the completely bounded COR conjecture for homomorphisms into matrices of order at most three; disprove the complete COR conjecture for arbitrary operator algebras with a three-dimensional example; and give the sharp complete bound for matrix subalgebras containing the diagonal in any matrix order.
events.revisions: v1 27 Aug 2026 (38 KB); v2 1 Sep 2026; v3 9 Sep 2026; v4 21 Sep 2026 (the version shown).
events.delivers: The complete (matrix-valued) Crouzeix inequality with constant 2 for matrices of order at most three. A complete bound implies the scalar bound for those orders; that step is my inference, not the paper's statement. The disproof concerns the complete COR conjecture for arbitrary operator algebras, which is a different conjecture from Crouzeix's.
events.remains: The complete Crouzeix inequality, and therefore the scalar statement as worded in the problem, for matrices of order four and above.
events.direction: For orders up to three, cuts toward the conjecture. The three-dimensional counterexample is to the complete COR conjecture, not to Crouzeix's.
events.object: The three-dimensional counterexample to the complete COR conjecture for arbitrary operator algebras has a target matrix of order two. The abstract does not give it explicitly, and I did not read the full text.

events.what_happened: Catalin Badea, Ryan O'Loughlin and Jani Virtanen post 'On the abstract approach to spectral constants: a proof of the Clouâtre–Ostermann–Ransford conjecture' (arXiv:2609.03637, submitted 3 September 2026). The abstract claims a proof of the abstract COR conjecture for a bounded unital homomorphism from a uniform algebra into matrices, paired with an antilinear map, under contractivity of the symmetrised map, with norm at most two. The proof uses positivity of real parts, an operator-valued Herglotz theorem, and the perturbation lemma of Lorist and Schwenninger.
events.delivers: The abstract COR conjecture with bound 2, for homomorphisms into matrices and into bounded operators on a Hilbert space, without requiring the antilinear map to be contractive. Whether this implies the Crouzeix statement is not stated on the page I read.
events.remains: Whether the COR result implies the constant-2 Crouzeix statement for W(A). A search snippet says a 2023 COR paper's bound would settle Crouzeix's conjecture on numerical ranges; I did not open that paper, so the implication is unverified.
events.direction: A neighbouring conjecture (COR) in the abstract setting. It uses the Lorist–Schwenninger lemma, and its bearing on the Crouzeix statement is open in this record.

events.what_happened: A Preprints.org manuscript 'Rigidity at the Extremal Crouzeix Constant' (manuscript 202609.0079; posted 1 September 2026, per a search summary). The summary says it characterises when ψ(A) = 2: only when the numerical range is a nondegenerate closed disk, using equality conditions of a sharp double-layer estimate, a Blaschke-product extremiser, and a rational extremiser whose unit lemniscate matches the boundary of W(A). The summary also says the scalar conjecture 'was proved by Jin, and independently by Lorist and Schwenninger'. The page returned HTTP 403, so none of this is checked, and the author is not identified.
events.delivers: Per the search summary only: a characterisation of the equality case ψ(A) = 2. It does not, on that summary, establish the inequality itself.
events.remains: The inequality is not settled by this item on the summary's account. I could not read it.
events.doubts: Unread. The summary is the only source, and its wording on equality conditions is ambiguous.
events.direction: Equality case of the sharp inequality, if the summary is right. Not checked.

events.what_happened: The GitHub repository tadamcz/crouzeix (owner Tom Adamczewski) posts a Lean 4 formalisation and exposition of the sharp scalar Crouzeix inequality for polynomials: for every complex n×n matrix A and every scalar complex polynomial p, ‖p(A)‖₂ ≤ 2 · max over W(A) of |p|. The README calls the work a 'rediscovery' made 'without obtaining the 2026 proof texts', says it has 'no claim to the first proof or first Lean formalization', and says the repository 'was machine-written by AI assistants at the direction of Tom Adamczewski'. Its exposition 'has not received human expert review'.
events.revisions: Three commits, all dated 9 Sep 2026 on the commits page. The README describes the output as 'generated by GPT-6 Astra in a September 2026 evaluation'.
events.delivers: Per the README: the polynomial case (finite matrices, scalar-valued functions) with constant 2, in Lean 4. The README says the final theorem 'also treats continuous, interior-analytic functions with a specified polynomial-limit functional calculus', and that 'the complete matrix-valued spectral-set conjecture is not asserted'. The README does not claim rational or general holomorphic functions.
events.remains: The complete matrix-valued form, which the README does not assert. General holomorphic f beyond the stated extension class; the README does not state that class precisely enough to decide.
events.doubts: The repository contains one sorry, in Challenge.lean; the README says the proved theorems do not depend on it. The README also says 'Comparator has not been rerun after packaging', and the axiom audit is recorded in a local-verification.txt file I did not see. No literal #print axioms output is shown. The exposition has no human expert review. The work is by its own description a rediscovery of results announced days earlier (see ai).
events.direction: Proves the constant-2 inequality for polynomials, cutting toward the conjecture, and says it re-derives a result already claimed by Jin and by Lorist and Schwenninger, which the agent was told about.

events.what_happened: Michel Crouzeix and Anne Greenbaum post 'Update to: Spectral sets: Numerical range and beyond' (arXiv:2609.22460, submitted 18 September 2026; v2 23 September 2026), using the results of Lorist and Schwenninger to update their 2019 SIMAX paper. Per the abstract: the regions considered there are K-spectral with smaller bounds than in 2019; various annular regions are 2-spectral; a convex region with a circular hole or cutout is 4-spectral.

events.remains: The constant-2 statement for W(A) is not an output of this paper, and the page does not claim it.

events.what_happened: Two OpenAI preprints, each citing the other, both claim the complete numerical-range inequality with constant 2: for a matrix-valued F = Σ B_k z^k, ‖F[A]‖ ≤ 2 max over z in W(A) of ‖F(z)‖, where F[A] = Σ A^k ⊗ B_k. A scalar f is the m = 1 case. (1) "A direct proof of the complete Crouzeix inequality" (dated 26 September 2026) proves this for every finite base dimension n, coefficient dimension m and degree d, for matrix polynomials only. Its route: for a bounded convex domain Ω containing W(A), with regular real-analytic boundary, any matrix polynomial F with ‖F‖ ≤ 1 on ∂Ω satisfies ‖F[A]‖ ≤ 2 (Theorem 'domain'). This uses singular-vector duality, Faber-coefficient estimates, and a positivity comparison of a 2×2 block built from the resolvent of A. Analytic convex outer approximations (Lemma 'approx') then shrink Ω to W(A), which covers point and segment ranges. (2) "The complete Crouzeix theorem: optimal similarity and a common positive boundary representation" (dated 23 September 2026) claims the same inequality for matrix polynomials over finite matrices (Corollary 'polynomial') and for every bounded operator on an arbitrary complex Hilbert space, with no separability assumption (Corollary 'hilbert'). It extends the bound to matrix-valued F holomorphic on an open neighbourhood of K = closure of W(A), with ‖F[A]‖ ≤ 2 max over K of ‖F‖, and to rational functions with poles outside K, which it calls a complete 2-spectral set. The Hilbert case reduces to a finite-dimensional compression, with W(A_E) ⊂ W(A). The holomorphic case uses Runge approximation and a contour form of the holomorphic calculus. Its polynomial bound runs through its structural theorems: for an analytic convex Ω containing W(A), it constructs a metric whose similarity S has ‖S‖‖S⁻¹‖ = κ ≤ 2, making S f(A) S⁻¹ a contraction, and a continuous positive density Λ of mass I representing v[A'] for every matrix-valued v holomorphic near Ω̄ (Theorems 'structural' and 'representation'). Both manuscripts give the same 2×2 nilpotent example to show that the constant 2 cannot be lowered.
events.delivers: For the list's statement (operator norm of f(A), A any complex square matrix, supremum over W(A) of |f|, constant exactly 2): the second manuscript claims all of it for f holomorphic on an open neighbourhood of W(A). In finite dimensions W(A) is compact, so this is the same as a neighbourhood of its closure. The scalar case is m = 1, and the claim is stated uniformly over n, m and d. The second manuscript's claims also reach infinite-dimensional operators, which the list does not ask for. The first manuscript delivers only the polynomial case: for every finite matrix A and every matrix polynomial P, ‖P[A]‖ ≤ 2 sup over W(A) of ‖P‖, with 2 sharp. It does not state the holomorphic or rational cases. Neither manuscript covers the list's full class, 'every function for which f(A) is defined'. Both restrict to polynomials, rational functions, or functions holomorphic near W(A). Both abstracts say the result 'resolves the complete Crouzeix conjecture', meaning the matrix-valued form, which contains the scalar conjecture. The manuscripts attribute the scalar constant-2 proofs to earlier 2026 preprints by Jin, by Lorist and Schwenninger, and by Luo.
events.remains: If the claims are correct, the list's inequality is covered for holomorphic f on a neighbourhood of W(A). Not covered: functions for which f(A) is defined but which are not holomorphic (or rational) near W(A). The matrix-valued, completely bounded form is claimed but is not part of the list's statement. The similarity and common-density results are claimed only for analytic convex domains containing W(A), not for W(A) itself, and they are not needed for the list's inequality. The first manuscript leaves the holomorphic and rational cases and infinite-dimensional operators open; the second manuscript addresses them.

machine_checked.scope:
The complete Crouzeix inequality bounds a matrix-valued polynomial evaluated at a matrix by its maximum norm on the numerical range. The formalized result proves the bound with constant $2$ for every positive matrix and coefficient size, every polynomial degree, and arbitrary complex coefficients. It also proves that no smaller universal constant works. Normality of the matrix and nonempty interior of its numerical range are not assumed.

The formalization proves the complete Crouzeix inequality with sharp constant two for every bounded operator on an arbitrary complex Hilbert space. For every matrix-valued polynomial, its operator evaluation has norm at most twice its supremum norm on the numerical range. The same bound holds for finite matrix-valued functions holomorphic near the closure of the numerical range and for rational functions with poles outside that closure. No separability assumption is required.

For finite matrices in a bounded convex domain with regular real-analytic Jordan boundary, the structural result gives an attained optimal similarity with condition number at most two and one continuous positive boundary density of mass the identity representing every matrix-valued analytic test. The linked supporting statements include numerical-range geometry and finite-compression identities.

events.doubts: (a) The first manuscript does not write out the step from polynomials to holomorphic functions, which the list's f requires. The second manuscript does write it out. (b) The second manuscript's polynomial bound, and so its Hilbert-space and holomorphic bounds, depends on its structural chain: the κ ≤ 2 comparison (Lemma 'comparison'), fed by the endpoint extremal (Proposition 'extremal'). Two steps there are compressed. One is the removal of apparent poles on the circle for the disk function F_D. The other is the unitary realization, which the text attributes to classical interpolation and colligation results while saying its endpoint data and realization are 'established here'. The first manuscript gives a separate route to the polynomial inequality, which the text says is a separate complete proof path. (c) The rational-function claim in Corollary 'hilbert' is argued in one paragraph (resolvent identity, differentiation in the pole, partial fractions), not in full. (d) The Gaussian outer approximation (Lemma 'gaussian') and the conformal reflection and patching appendices in both manuscripts are compressed. They cite Ahlfors, Pommerenke and Carathéodory's theorem for the classical steps. (e) The two manuscripts cite each other. The first cites the second for 'counterparts' to its calculations. The second cites the first for an alternative outer approximation and for calculations it says it re-proves. Each says its own proof path is complete. (f) The sharpness and holomorphic claims are stated for the same constant 2 as the polynomial claim, so any doubt about the polynomial bound carries over to them.
events.direction: proves the conjecture (constant 2 holds and is sharp); the first manuscript proves the polynomial case only
events.object: A sharpness witness, not a counterexample to the inequality: the 2×2 nilpotent matrix A = [[0,2],[0,0]] with f(z) = z (scalar, m = 1). Here ‖A‖ = 2, while the maximum of |z| over W(A) is 1, so no constant below 2 works. The matrix is explicit. Both manuscripts give it.

disputes.summary: Jin's manuscript is first in the record (v1 posted 27 July 2026). Lorist and Schwenninger say their AI exploration ran on 25–26 July and that they learned of Jin's reference only on 28 July, so they present their proof as independent. Secondary sources repeat 'independent' without checking the footnote. The tadamcz repository calls its own work a rediscovery and claims no priority.

Whether Jin's manuscript discloses AI use. The Breakthrough Tracker says 'No AI disclosure was located on the inspected public page for Jin's concurrent manuscript'. The ingenieur.de and Magica reports, paraphrasing the preprint's own statements, say ChatGPT is credited with the central sampling or Herglotz-kernel idea and with writing, references and typesetting, and that Jin takes responsibility for the mathematics. The preprint could not be opened, so these cannot be reconciled. Versions may differ.

The same model is named differently. The Lorist–Schwenninger v2 text says 'GPT-5.6 Sol Pro'; their v1 text says 'ChatGPT 5.6 Pro by OpenAI'. Secondary sources say 'GPT-5.6 Sol', 'GPT-5.6', 'ChatGPT', or 'OpenAI's latest reasoning model'. Strings are recorded as each source wrote them.

The date of the Townsend–Greenbaum SIAM News essay: 11 August 2026 on the alextownsend.net essays listing, 14 August on Wikipedia, and 15 August in the MathWorld reference and a Remio article. The essay PDF was not readable to me, so this is unresolved.

The class of f each claim covers differs. Jin: polynomials in v1, reportedly all holomorphic f near W(A) in later versions (snippets only). Lorist and Schwenninger: rational f with poles outside the closure of W(A), for bounded Hilbert-space operators. Luo: polynomials and rational functions without poles on W(A). The statement says only 'a complex function f'. Whether the rational theorem extends to all holomorphic f by a limit argument is not shown in the text I read.
Jin's manuscript appears as 'The Numerical Range Is a 2-Spectral Set' (v1 title, Preprints.org) and as 'The Crouzeix Conjecture' (Breakthrough Tracker record). Later items cite the first title.

The tadamcz/crouzeix README attributes its Lean proof to 'GPT-6 Astra', which the Lean repository calls generated 'in a September 2026 evaluation'. A search report says 'Astra' is an unofficial name, so the string is recorded as the README gives it. The same owner's Köthe-conjecture work, which a search snippet credits to the same model name, concerns a different problem and is not researched here.

summary: I found no peer-reviewed resolution of the constant-2 inequality. Three unrefereed 2026 preprints claim it. Jin's preprint (Preprints.org, first posted 27 July 2026) I could not open, since every Preprints.org fetch returned HTTP 403; its account rests on secondary reports (ingenieur.de, Magica, Wick's blog, Remio, the Breakthrough Tracker) and on search snippets. Lorist and Schwenninger's arXiv:2608.03841 (4 August 2026) I read through the arXiv HTML of v2 and the v1 abstract. Its theorem covers bounded Hilbert-space operators and rational f with poles outside the closure of W(A), so it covers matrices of every size but not all holomorphic f on the face of it. Luo's Preprints.org manuscript (late August 2026) I know only from its abstract as relayed in snippets, plus a third-party README. Partial 2026 results: Åhag, Czyż and Virtanen (arXiv:2608.27346, 27 August) settle the complete form for matrices of order at most three, and Badea, O'Loughlin and Virtanen (arXiv:2609.03637, 3 September) prove the abstract COR conjecture, whose bearing on the Crouzeix statement is not established in what I read. A Lean 4 repository (tadamcz/crouzeix, 9 September 2026) formalises the polynomial case, describes itself as a rediscovery, and attributes its proof to 'GPT-6 Astra'. Crouzeix and Greenbaum's 18 September update uses the Lorist–Schwenninger result as an input. The prior best constant was 1+√2 (Crouzeix–Palencia, arXiv February 2017). The 2024–2025 items (Malman et al. twice, Crouzeix–Greenbaum on weighted-shift matrices, Crouzeix on unbounded convex cases) moved neighbouring quantities or restricted classes, and none reaches 2 for W(A). The 2026 results are therefore: a full claim of the constant-2 inequality for polynomials (Jin, Luo, the Lean repo) and for rational functions (Lorist–Schwenninger), with the originator and two expert co-authors reportedly checking Jin's argument informally; no journal or referee report; and a Simons Institute whiteboard dated November 2025 (date inferred from the URL) still describing the conjecture as open. AI involvement: the authors of Lorist–Schwenninger say a model (GPT-5.6 Sol Pro) was used to explore strategies, and that it supplied a key observation leading to Lemma 1, but that the final proof was developed, verified and written by the authors. That is a claim of load-bearing contribution in their own words, to be weighed by the judging pass. For Jin, I could not obtain the authors' own sentence. Secondary reports say the preprint credits ChatGPT with the central sampling idea, and the Tracker says no disclosure was found on the page it inspected, so per DEEP_DIVE §5.4 I did not list a system in ai.systems for Jin; the ai block records that a system is named but unquoted. For the Lean repository, the owner's own README says the Lean proof was written by GPT-6 Astra, which is recorded. For Luo, the only AI statement is a third-party description of the preprint. Pre-2026 partial results and the 2024–2025 items are recorded as events, with dates taken from first public versions. Minor discrepancies are noted in disputes: the Malman et al. 2024 journal (IMRN versus Integral Equations and Operator Theory), the essay date, and model names. Also, a search summary attributed a settled 'scalar' result to Åhag, Czyż and Virtanen. Their abstract does not say that, so I did not record it as an event. I did not pursue the OpenAI Cycle Double Cover claim of July 2026, which concerns a different problem.
competing_reading: Read the record as established. Two independent proofs of the scalar constant-2 inequality exist: Jin (27 July) and Lorist–Schwenninger (4 August), whose AI exploration preceded their learning of Jin's work. The originator and expert co-authors reportedly checked Jin's argument. Luo and a Lean polynomial formalisation agree, and Crouzeix and Greenbaum now build on the Lorist–Schwenninger result. On this reading the polynomial and rational scalar case was settled by August–September 2026, and the judging pass should count the earliest verified route rather than wait for refereeing. The complex-f class in the statement is then covered by the rational theorem plus a standard limiting argument, which I did not check.
what_would_settle_it: (1) A journal acceptance or written referee report for Lorist–Schwenninger (five pages) and for Jin's preprint. (2) The text of Jin's latest version (Preprints.org v4, DOI 10.20944/preprints202607.1919.v4), to check the holomorphic-f claim, the scope, the AI declaration and any Lean link. (3) A Lean build with #print axioms on Luo's and Jin's repositories, and a sorry check on the tadamcz repository's proved theorems. (4) Whether the Lorist–Schwenninger rational theorem extends to all holomorphic f, which decides whether the statement's complex-f class is covered. (5) The Townsend–Greenbaum essay text (its date, and what the authors say about the AI run and about who checked the proof). (6) Whether the Badea–O'Loughlin–Virtanen COR result implies the scalar inequality for W(A).

event.what_happened: Shanmu Jin posts 'The Numerical Range Is a 2-Spectral Set' on Preprints.org (DOI 10.20944/preprints202607.1919.v1; submitted 24 July, posted 27 July 2026). Per its abstract as relayed by search snippets, for every complex polynomial p and n×n matrix A, ‖p(A)‖ ≤ 2 · max over W(A) of |p|, so W(A) is a 2-spectral set; the author claims this proves Crouzeix's conjecture and that the constant is optimal. Later versions (v3 5 Aug, v4 7 Aug) are reported to extend the estimate to every f holomorphic near W(A). I could not open any version: every Preprints.org fetch returned HTTP 403. The account below therefore rests on secondary reports that paraphrase the preprint and on snippets. The author is reported as a neurosurgery resident and postdoctoral researcher at Peking Union Medical College Hospital with no formal mathematics training.
event.revisions: v1 posted 27 Jul 2026 (title 'The Numerical Range Is a 2-Spectral Set'); v3 5 Aug 2026; v4 7 Aug 2026, cited by ingenieur.de as the current version. Breakthrough Tracker lists the manuscript as 'The Crouzeix Conjecture', revised through 7 Aug. Scope changed between versions per snippets (polynomials in v1; holomorphic f later).
event.delivers: Per the abstract as relayed: the constant-2 inequality for every polynomial p and every n×n A, so the numerical range is a 2-spectral set, and the constant is claimed optimal. Central tool as relayed: a positive-real completion theorem, and a matrix-valued Herglotz kernel evaluated at specially chosen points that cancels the completion term. Per snippets, later versions claim every f holomorphic near W(A).
event.remains: Nothing, on the author's claim. Whether the holomorphic-f extension is in the preprint I could not check.

judgement.why: The statement's 'complex function f' is read as the standard conjecture (f holomorphic near W(A)); since W(A) is compact and convex, polynomials are uniformly dense in that class (Runge), so a constant-2 proof for all polynomials, or for rational functions, settles the whole statement — hence Jin, Lorist–Schwenninger, Luo, the tadamcz Lean polynomial proof and the OpenAI manuscripts are all scored whole. Jin is the one 2026 event scored digested: Crouzeix, Townsend and Greenbaum are named and reported publicly (SIAM News essay, quoted on Wick's blog) to have checked the proof, which clears the bar even though it reaches this record secondhand; it is marked doubtful for that reason and the author's background, not set aside. Lorist–Schwenninger's praise and downstream use by Crouzeix–Greenbaum are engagement, not a reading, so unreviewed. Lorist–Schwenninger is assisted rather than none: the authors' own declaration says the model's key observation yielded a preliminary result from which Lemma 1 was abstracted, which is mathematics in the result. Jin and Luo get none because no first-party AI quote is recorded in their systems. Malman et al.'s domain-dependent improvement, Crouzeix's unbounded case, q-numerical ranges, COR and the 2026 annular update are variants; the per-N Crouzeix ratio is a bound; Crouzeix–Greenbaum 2025 re-proves a known class (none). The OpenAI 2×2 nilpotent sharpness example is a witness to the constant being exactly 2.
judgement.doubts: Secondary reports say Jin's preprint credits ChatGPT with the central Herglotz-kernel/sampling idea; if that disclosure is confirmed, Jin's event would be assisted or generated, but no first-party quote exists in the record, so it is answered none. Jin's digested rests on secondhand accounts of an unreadable essay; a stricter reading gives unreviewed. The literal statement ('any complex function for which f(A) is defined') is broader than holomorphic; scored on the standard reading. Badea–O'Loughlin–Virtanen may imply the scalar inequality via COR, unestablished in the record.
